messages.subject: Re: Problem executing R functions from JAVA
messages.subject_clean: Problem executing R functions from JAVA
messages.body_plain:
Hi Rajib,
Regarding the NoClassDefFoundError, it looks like you need to upgrade your JRE to Java 7: java.util.Objects is a new addition to the Java API.

I believe that Renjin's documentation explicitly requires Java 1.6+, so that's something we need to update.

Regarding the corrplot package. You need to make sure that this library is on your classpath. If you run Renjin interactively from the REPL, this package and it's dependencies will be automatically downloaded, but if you're embedding Renjin in your application, you need to manage the classpath yourself. For example, if you're using maven, then you can include corrplot in your pom.xml file:

<dependencies>
  <dependency>
    <groupId>org.renjin.cran</groupId>
    <artifactId>corrplot</artifactId>
    <version>0.73-b213</version>
  </dependency>
</dependencies>
<repositories>
  <repository>
    <id>bedatadriven</id>
    <name>bedatadriven public repo</name>
    <url>http://nexus.bedatadriven.com/content/groups/public/</url>
  </repository>
</repositories>
If you're using gradle, then you would use something like

dependencies {
   compile "org.renjin.cran:corrplot:0.73-b213"
}

But also keep in mind that Renjin does not currently implement any of the graphics functionality of R, so this might not be of very much use to you.

Best,
Alex

messages.body_plain:
Not directly, at least at the moment. You'd have to create a class in Java/scala/etc which delegates to a RenjinScriptEngine instance.

It would be possible to add an automatic step that could create a proxy for an interface, or generate a class on demand for an R object, but we'd need to think about how exactly you would define methods for a Java class in R. A list of functions? Should it wrap an S3/S4 object?

Proposals welcome!

Alex

messages.body_plain:
Hi Rajib,

After your first email, I did a quick check with the animal-sniffer maven plugin:
http://eclipsesource.com/blogs/2014/05/09/ensure-class-library-compatibility-in-a-maven-build/

To see just to what degree we depend on Java 7 at this point, and found only a handful of references. The source of the error from your call to cor(), for example,
is our implementation of identical(), which is the only reference to java.lang.Objects I found:
https://github.com/bedatadriven/renjin/blob/master/core/src/main/java/org/renjin/primitives/Identical.java#L137-137

This is a pretty widely used R function so I'd imagine not much will run without hitting this.

I'd be happy to accept a pull request replacing these with suitable calls to Java 1.6-only APIs, but I'm not sure how much time this will buy you:
We're currently working on a new version of the C/Fortran compiler that uses new Java 7 bytecodes pretty extensively, and then you won't be able to run Renjin at all with a JRE < 1.7.

Can you tell me more about the application in which you're trying to embed Renjin? Is there a reason you can't just run the application on a new version of the JRE?

messages.subject: Re: Roadmap
messages.body_plain:
Hi Rodrigo,

Indeed, we're approaching development very iteratively, but we've set out big some milestones for ourselves with the aim of supporting our research partners in the Horizon 2020 Sound Project (http://www.sound-biomed.eu/).

Roughly speaking, we're looking at a few big milestones over the coming months:

1) Basic support for S4 (released!)
2) Support for .Call interface to better support packages with extensive C code, including survival, limma, and forecast. (in progress <https://github.com/bedatadriven/renjin/commits/wip-dot-call>)
3) Full support for common, complex genomics workflows (see https://github.com/bedatadriven/genbench)

We've made some good progress on the first two milestones, which are pretty big chunks of new development, while the third milestone will involve more little bug fixes to clean up any differences between Renjin and GNU R 3.2 that affect the workflows in genbench.

Once we're able to run all of these packages and workflows on Renjin, we'll turn back to focusing on performance improvements, hopefully by the beginning of 2016.

We'll continue the continuous delivery model that we've put into place over the last year -- so we'll release any fix or change that passes all tests as they're finished.

Hope this helps!

Alex

messages.subject: Re: Roadmap
messages.body_plain:
Yes, indeed, I think the .Call and a better C compiler are the last "big" things we need to finish in order to get "most" packages running on Renjin.

Regarding graphics, it's something we're definitely not tackling ourselves at least in the short term, but would be excited to see someone else take it up.

I think one approach that could be interesting would be to explore implementing the existing R graphics API in pure R, and make graphicsDevice a simple S3 or S4 object with just a few methods. (One of implementation of which could just call out to java.awt.Graphics$new() to handle most image formats). Having a clean code base in R might make experimentation with Js backends easier.

There's a few projects out there looking at alternative APIs / implementations of graphics for R, like:
https://github.com/deepayan/tessella
https://github.com/deepayan/yagpack
https://github.com/ggobi/qtpaint
https://github.com/ggobi/cranvas

Many of these libraries define a limited number of primitives which are implemented in C using bindings to Qt, and would be straightfoward to replace with equivalent primitives binding to java.awt. That's in contrast to the base graphics package which is mostly written in C and is quite sprawling.

But in any case, would love to hear what you're working on with MDArray, so please share updates here!

Best,
Alex
